title: Clinical Mastery: Congenital Eyelid Coloboma
summary: An in-depth guide to the identification, associations, and surgical management of congenital eyelid colobomas, focusing on ocular safety and functional restoration. This guide bridges core clinical questions with surgical pearls for the practicing ophthalmologist.

sections.title: Clinical Presentation & Diagnosis
sections.content: Scenario 1: 1. What does the picture show? The picture shows a coloboma of the upper eyelid where the eyelid is fused to the globe. 2. What is the diagnosis? Congenital Coloboma of the Eyelid (eyelid cleft or notch). Scenario 2: Q1: Describe the picture. (Note: Clinical diagnosis is consistent with Congenital Eyelid Coloboma, characterized by a full-thickness defect of the eyelid margin).

sections.title: Management & Monitoring
content: Step 1: Monitor infant for exposure keratopathy due to the eyelid defect.
Step 2: Perform surgical closure of the eyelid defect (required in most cases).
Step 3: For defects < 1/3 eyelid: Create raw vertical margins and slide flaps along the eyelid crease.
Step 4: Use lateral cantholysis if additional horizontal relaxation is needed.
Step 5: For large defects: Utilize a variation of the lateral canthal semicircular flap technique.
Step 6: Avoid eyelid-sharing procedures that occlude the visual axis to prevent amblyopia.

sections.title: Clinical Pearls & Red Flags
content: Exposure Keratopathy: High risk in infants with eyelid coloboma.
Amblyopia: Significant risk if visual axis is occluded.
True Coloboma Definition: Must involve a defect in the eyelid margin.
Surgical Priority: Protect the visual axis at all costs during reconstruction.

sections.title: Investigation Workup & Assessment
content: Complete ocular examination to rule out co-existing ocular colobomas.
Systemic assessment for facial clefts and syndrome screening (Goldenhar).
Assessment of lacrimal system patency, especially in lower lid defects.
Baseline corneal assessment for signs of drying or epithelial defects.
